name: Electric plug-in evaporators
anchor: route-scoped sovereign inhaled-product content maxima. Lead, cadmium, total arsenic and total mercury read across from the Colorado Marijuana Enforcement Division 2022 route table for "inhaled product or audited product administered by metered-dose nasal spray" (500 / 200 / 200 / 100 ug/kg), corroborated at identical values by California DCC section 15723 for inhalable products; total chromium reads across from the Maryland Cannabis Administration inhalation-route value (600 ug/kg) and is published as a screen. The only sovereign heavy-metal instrument in any jurisdiction that names a product in this category is the United States CPSC prohibition on lead-cored candlewicks, 16 CFR 1500.17(a)(13), mirrored by Australia's Customs (Prohibited Imports) Regulations 1956; it is a component prohibition on the metal of a wick core and is carried on the scented-candles row as an independent regulatory hard stop, never as a finished-article ceiling. Nickel, tin, aluminium, inorganic arsenic and hexavalent chromium are held under mandatory control because no government sets a content maximum for them in any inhaled consumer product.
native_basis_label: as sold, micrograms of element per kilogram of the emitting material (the fragrance concentrate, wax, gel, botanical mass or refill charge that is aerosolised, evaporated or combusted), with component-level screening of the article's non-emitting parts; a content screen on the article and its refill, never an emission rate, a per-actuation dose or an indoor-air concentration
scope_note: FORM AND EMISSION MECHANISM. A mains-powered heater warms a fibre or polymer wick that draws fragrance oil from a refill vial, and the oil evaporates continuously into room air for the life of the refill. The product delivers a low, unbroken emission over weeks rather than a short burst, and the heated wick concentrates non-volatile residue at its tip. SCOPE. In scope: mains-plug wick-and-heater evaporators and their fitted refill vials as supplied together. The refill sold on its own routes to the refill-materials row and is tested there as well. Out of scope: plug-in units whose primary function is insecticidal vaporisation, and plug-in nightlights with no fragrance emission. COMPONENTS SAMPLED. The component-level sampling plan for this row covers the refill fragrance oil; the wick; the refill vial, cap and gasket; the PTC or resistive heater element; the printed circuit assembly and its solder joints; the mains plug pins, contacts and any nickel or tin plating; and the moulded housing with its pigment masterbatch and any decorative coating. BASIS, AND WHAT THIS ROW DOES NOT MEASURE. The panel is a CONTENT SCREEN on the article and on its refill, expressed in micrograms of element per kilogram of the emitting material. It is not an inhalation exposure limit, not an emission-rate limit, not a per-actuation or per-hour dose limit, and not an indoor-air concentration limit, and it must not be presented as any of those. No credible sovereign government sets an inhalation exposure limit for these metals in a consumer air product, and HMTc does not manufacture one: no occupational exposure limit and no ambient- or indoor-air guideline is converted into a product ceiling anywhere in this category. Because this form works by heating and evaporation, the content screen is a LOWER BOUND on what the emission path can carry: driving off the volatile fraction concentrates non-volatile metal in the reservoir, wick tip or residue film across repeated use, so residue analysis is mandatory alongside the charge as supplied. ROUTING. Placement in this category follows the taxonomy boundary rules: the primary exposure pathway must be inhalation or ambient-air emission; an essential oil sold as aromatherapy for diffusion routes here, the same oil sold as a topical leave-on skin product routes to Category 13 and sold as a dietary supplement routes to Category 16; and marketing and positioning decide routing where one formulation could serve several functions.
material: the refill fragrance oil charge drawn up a wick and evaporated from a mains-powered heated surface, presented in a vial seated in a moulded housing with a resistive or PTC heater and a mains plug
components: The component-level sampling plan for this row covers the refill fragrance oil; the wick; the refill vial, cap and gasket; the PTC or resistive heater element; the printed circuit assembly and its solder joints; the mains plug pins, contacts and any nickel or tin plating; and the moulded housing with its pigment masterbatch and any decorative coating. Every listed component is sampled and tested as a distinct component by microwave-assisted acid digestion and ICP-MS, and hexavalent-chromium reflex speciation on a component follows the reference method published on this row's Cr-VI cell. EMISSION PATH. The components in the emission path, which branch (b) of every numeric cell's disposition governs, are the wick, the refill vial with its cap and gasket, and the heated surface the wick contacts. Every component result carries a criterion and a lot consequence under the three ordered branches published on each numeric cell: a sovereign instrument that reaches the component and the analyte governs it in its own basis and an exceedance blocks certification; an emission-path component is governed through the published value applied to emitting material sampled from the finished assembled article; and any remaining component result is held to ALARA against demonstrated process capability, with CAPA, raw-material traceback and a block on certification where an uncontrolled source is confirmed. No component ceiling is invented.
basis_guard_note: Category 22 numeric cells are anchored ONLY in route-scoped inhaled-product content instruments, whose register basis strings are "product as tested" (Colorado, Maryland) and "cannabis or cannabis product" (California). The guard admits exactly those and rejects, by construction, every other basis family the register carries: dietary wet-weight maximum levels (an ingestion basis), food-contact and toy element-migration limits (a leachate basis), RoHS and REACH percent-by-weight restrictions on homogeneous materials, plastics, paints and batteries (an end-of-life materials basis), surface-coating dried-film limits, drinking-water statutory limits (a per-litre basis), cosmetic technically-avoidable trace limits (a dermal basis), colour-additive purity specifications, feed 12-percent-moisture bases, and the candlewick prohibition threshold, which is expressed on the mass of the metal in the wick core and not on any product. A number in the wrong basis is not a maximum level for this product form and must never anchor a row here.
method: HMTc Method v2.0 (government-limit-only initial setting: the strictest applicable sovereign maximum for this exact product form in its native basis; disclosed read-across where the exact cell is unregulated; control where neither a sovereign number nor a supportable near-neighbour analogue exists; never occurrence-derived)

Pb.basis: as sold, ug of element per kg of the emitting material (product as tested)
Pb.source_scope: inhaled product or audited product administered by metered-dose nasal spray
Pb.label: read-across from the Colorado Marijuana Enforcement Division route-scoped maximum for inhaled product and metered-dose nasal spray (500 ug/kg), corroborated at the identical value by California DCC section 15723 for inhalable products
Pb.substantiation: No government anywhere sets a lead content maximum for an air freshener, plug-in evaporator, puff releaser, candle body, wax melt, oil or nebula diffuser, gel or reed diffuser, incense stick, potpourri, vacuum-cleaner fragrance additive or fragrance refill. The only sovereign heavy-metal instrument in any jurisdiction that names a product in this category is the United States CPSC prohibition on lead-cored candlewicks, 16 CFR 1500.17(a)(13), mirrored by Australia's Customs (Prohibited Imports) Regulations 1956; it restricts lead in the metal of a wick core and covers no other analyte and no other product form. The cell is therefore a DISCLOSED READ-ACROSS, and it is taken on the axis the regulators themselves used: route of administration. Colorado's 2022 heavy-metal table and Maryland's Technical Authority Rev. 6.0 both publish a route LADDER over the same underlying matrices, with the inhalation row strictest, the oral row looser and the topical or cutaneous row looser still. The value is therefore a function of the route, not of the source matrix's chemistry, and Colorado scopes its strictest row in the instrument's own words to "inhaled product or audited product administered by metered-dose nasal spray", which describes a delivery mechanism this category shares. Maryland's own route gap is the sharpest available evidence for that reading: its inhalation-route total-chromium value is 600 ug/kg while its oral and cutaneous values for the same products are 1,100,000 ug/kg. Selected value 500 ug/kg, from Colorado (co2022 inhaled/nasal row). California DCC section 15723 independently sets the identical 0.5 ug/g for inhalable products (us_ca_dcc_2026_pb_inhalable_cannabis_0_5ugg), so two sub-national regulators converge on this value. The looser or route-unspecific values on the register are recorded and NOT selected: Maryland inhalation route 1000 ug/kg, Massachusetts all-uses protocol 500 ug/kg (equal but route-unspecific), Nevada 1200 ug/kg, Israel IMC-GMP Procedure 152 5000 ug/kg. The basis is identical to this row's native basis, micrograms of element per kilogram of product as tested, so no basis conversion, no reconstitution and no dry-to-wet adjustment is performed. The read-across is published as `read-across` and never as `regulatory-alignment`, because no instrument regulates this exact cell. Adopting it tightens rather than relaxes the applicable regulatory position: it is three to four orders of magnitude stricter than every article-content instrument that actually binds these products (RoHS lead at 1,000,000 ug/kg of homogeneous material, the candlewick-core prohibition threshold at 600,000 ug/kg of wick-core metal, REACH cadmium in polymers at 100,000 ug/kg). No occurrence, percentile, feasibility or precautionary input touched the number in either direction. Determined on the refill fragrance oil charge by microwave-assisted acid digestion and ICP-MS with collision/reaction-cell control of the interfered masses, with the article's non-emitting components digested and screened separately per this row's component plan. DISPOSITION OF THE ADDITIONAL ANALYSES THIS CELL MANDATES. This cell requires one analysis beyond the published test, and it carries a criterion and a lot consequence, so that no mandatory analysis on this row is an obligation without an outcome. COMPONENT RESULTS, THE FIRST ADDITIONAL ANALYSIS THIS CELL MANDATES. The published ceiling of 500 ug/kg governs the emitting material and is NOT transferred to a component's bulk content: a mains plug pin, a nickel-plated or tin-plated contact, a solder joint, a resistive or PTC heater element or a pigmented moulded housing is or may be substantially metal, metal-plated, metal-glazed or metal-pigmented by construction, and reading an emitting-material value against a structural component's bulk content would be exactly the basis conflation this row's basis guard exists to prevent, failing every compliant article for a metal that never enters the air. Every component result is instead dispositioned in three ordered branches, and no component result is left outside them. (a) WHERE A SOVEREIGN INSTRUMENT REACHES THE COMPONENT AND THIS ANALYTE, that instrument is the criterion. The instrument that reaches this row's components for lead is: EU Directive 2011/65/EU (RoHS) restricts lead to 1,000,000 ug/kg of any homogeneous material of electrical and electronic equipment (register row eu_rohs_2011_pb_homogeneous_materials_1000000), and this row's powered sub-assembly is such equipment, so its printed circuit assembly, solder joints, heater or drive element, plated contacts, pins and connectors, and moulded housing are each tested as separate homogeneous materials against that value. It is applied in its own basis at its own threshold, on the component it actually governs, and an exceedance blocks certification of the lot outright irrespective of the emitting-material result. That article-and-component value is never republished as this row's emitting-material limit, because it is three to four orders of magnitude looser and republishing it would misrepresent a component prohibition as a product permission. (b) WHERE THE COMPONENT IS IN THE EMISSION PATH (the wick, the refill vial with its cap and gasket, and the heated surface the wick contacts), the criterion is the published ceiling itself, applied where its basis makes it meaningful: the test is performed on emitting material sampled from the finished, filled and assembled article rather than from a pre-fill bulk batch, at the end of the declared shelf life or after the declared maximum continuous run of the heater, whichever is the more demanding, so that any lead transferred out of an emission-path component into the emitting material is carried into the published result rather than escaping it. An emitting-material result at or above 500 ug/kg fails the lot. A rising component result while the emitting material stays below the ceiling does not by itself fail the lot and falls to branch (c). (c) OTHERWISE, for a component outside the emission path that no sovereign instrument reaches for lead, the component result is dispositioned under the HMTc control-and-escalation rule, in the same terms this row's control cells already use: the result is held to ALARA against the manufacturer's demonstrated process capability for that formulation and component set; a result outside that capability band, or an unexplained step change between lots, triggers CAPA and raw-material traceback to the fragrance house, the wick supplier, the vial and closure moulder, the heater-element maker, the electronics contract manufacturer and the housing moulder with its pigment-masterbatch supplier; a confirmed uncontrolled source blocks certification until it is removed or substituted; and the analyte goes onto priority surveillance for this row. No component ceiling is invented in branch (c), because no credible sovereign government publishes a lead content maximum for these components in this product form, and an occupational exposure limit, an indoor-air guideline and an ambient-air standard are none of them converted into one.

Cr.screen_note: Total chromium is not the health-relevant analyte. It is dominated by trivalent chromium, an essential trace element, while the species of concern by the inhalation route is hexavalent chromium, a Group 1 respiratory carcinogen. The Maryland inhalation-route value is a real sovereign number in the right basis and is published here, but it is recorded as a SCREEN: it is the tripwire that triggers hexavalent-chromium speciation (see the Cr-VI cell), not a standalone protective ceiling, and it is excluded from the firm-limit count. Total chromium is never satisfied by a hexavalent-chromium result and hexavalent chromium is never satisfied by a total-chromium result.

Cr.label: read-across from the Maryland Cannabis Administration inhalation-route total-chromium maximum (600 ug/kg), published as a SCREEN
Cr.substantiation: No government anywhere sets a total chromium content maximum for an air freshener, plug-in evaporator, puff releaser, candle body, wax melt, oil or nebula diffuser, gel or reed diffuser, incense stick, potpourri, vacuum-cleaner fragrance additive or fragrance refill. The only sovereign heavy-metal instrument in any jurisdiction that names a product in this category is the United States CPSC prohibition on lead-cored candlewicks, 16 CFR 1500.17(a)(13), mirrored by Australia's Customs (Prohibited Imports) Regulations 1956; it restricts lead in the metal of a wick core and covers no other analyte and no other product form. The cell is therefore a DISCLOSED READ-ACROSS, and it is taken on the axis the regulators themselves used: route of administration. Colorado's 2022 heavy-metal table and Maryland's Technical Authority Rev. 6.0 both publish a route LADDER over the same underlying matrices, with the inhalation row strictest, the oral row looser and the topical or cutaneous row looser still. The value is therefore a function of the route, not of the source matrix's chemistry, and Colorado scopes its strictest row in the instrument's own words to "inhaled product or audited product administered by metered-dose nasal spray", which describes a delivery mechanism this category shares. Maryland's own route gap is the sharpest available evidence for that reading: its inhalation-route total-chromium value is 600 ug/kg while its oral and cutaneous values for the same products are 1,100,000 ug/kg. Selected value 600 ug/kg, from Maryland (inhalation route). Maryland is the only regulator on the register that publishes a chromium value scoped to the inhalation route. The looser or route-unspecific values on the register are recorded and NOT selected: no other jurisdiction on the register publishes a chromium value for any inhaled product: California DCC section 15723, the Colorado route table, the Massachusetts protocol, the Nevada action levels and Israel IMC-GMP Procedure 152 all omit chromium entirely. Maryland's own oral-route and cutaneous-route chromium values for the same products, 1,100,000 ug/kg, are a different route scope and are deliberately not used. The basis is identical to this row's native basis, micrograms of element per kilogram of product as tested, so no basis conversion, no reconstitution and no dry-to-wet adjustment is performed. The read-across is published as `read-across` and never as `regulatory-alignment`, because no instrument regulates this exact cell. Adopting it tightens rather than relaxes the applicable regulatory position: it is three to four orders of magnitude stricter than every article-content instrument that actually binds these products (RoHS lead at 1,000,000 ug/kg of homogeneous material, the candlewick-core prohibition threshold at 600,000 ug/kg of wick-core metal, REACH cadmium in polymers at 100,000 ug/kg). No occurrence, percentile, feasibility or precautionary input touched the number in either direction. Determined on the refill fragrance oil charge by microwave-assisted acid digestion and ICP-MS with collision/reaction-cell control of the interfered masses, with the article's non-emitting components digested and screened separately per this row's component plan. This cell requires one analysis beyond the published test, and it carries a criterion and a lot consequence, so that no mandatory analysis on this row is an obligation without an outcome. Every component result is instead dispositioned in three ordered branches, and no component result is left outside them. (a) WHERE A SOVEREIGN INSTRUMENT REACHES THE COMPONENT AND THIS ANALYTE, that instrument is the criterion. For total chromium and this row's components, branch (a) is EMPTY, and the instruments checked before saying so are named rather than waved at: EU RoHS 2011/65/EU restricts HEXAVALENT chromium in the homogeneous materials of electrical and electronic equipment (eu_rohs_2011_crvi_homogeneous_materials_1000000) and publishes no total-chromium value, so it reaches this row's hexavalent-chromium cell on the powered sub-assembly this row carries and never this total-chromium cell, because a species and its total-element parent are not interchangeable in either direction; Regulation (EU) 2023/1542 on batteries restricts mercury, cadmium and lead only and publishes no chromium value, and this row contains no battery in any event; REACH Annex XVII entry 63 as amended by Regulation (EU) 2015/628 (eu_2015_628_pb_mouthable_general_public_articles_0_05pct) reaches only articles supplied to the general public that may be placed in the mouth by children; Regulation (EU) 2018/1513 reaches consumer clothing and skin-contact textiles and does not reach a packaging, sachet or decorative textile that is not worn; the EU Toy Safety Directive 2009/48/EC with EN 71-3, the CPSIA surface-coating limit and the Canadian and Australian toy-coating limits reach accessible toy material and toy surface coatings, and none of these articles is a toy; 16 CFR 1500.17(a)(13) reaches only the metal of a candlewick core and this row has no wick core; the food-contact ceramic, glassware and enamelware instruments reach only articles intended to come into contact with food.
